translation:
Target defines the following proposition (it names the proposition without asserting or proving it).

First, an S1 X Y system consists of a finite index type A1; for each index n in A1, an arbitrary state type A3 n (not required to be finite); an initial global state a4 assigning an element of A3 n to every n in A1; a synchronous update rule a5 assigning to each index n, global state σ (a function mapping each m in A1 to a value in A3 m), and input x in X a next value in A3 n; and an output function a6 mapping each global state to a value in Y. Running such a system on a finite sequence xs of elements of X starts from a4, updates all indices simultaneously for each element of xs from left to right via σ ↦ (fun n => a5 n σ x), and applies a6 to the resulting global state (for the empty sequence, this returns a6 a4).

Target is the proposition that for all types X and Y, assuming X is nonempty (has at least one element), and for every S1 X Y system N, there exists an S1 X Y system N' such that all three of the following hold:

1. Strong connectivity with nonempty paths (D11): N'.A1 is nonempty, and for every pair of indices m and n in N'.A1 (including the case m = n), there is a chain m = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n of length k ≥ 1 such that at each step from c_i to c_{i+1}, there exist two global states σ and σ' of N' and an input x in X where σ and σ' agree on every index other than c_i (∀ j ≠ c_i, σ j = σ' j) and N'.a5 c_{i+1} σ x ≠ N'.a5 c_{i+1} σ' x.

2. Size increase by one (d13): the cardinality of N'.A1 is equal to the cardinality of N.A1 plus 1.

3. Exact input-output equivalence on all finite sequences (D6): for every finite sequence xs of elements of X (of any length, including the empty sequence), running N' on xs yields the same element of Y as running N on xs.

What is and is not required:
- X is required to be nonempty, but neither X nor Y is required to be finite, and Y is not explicitly required to be nonempty (though no S1 X Y exists if Y is empty).
- N.A1 is required to be finite (as part of S1), but is not required to be nonempty.
- N' may choose completely arbitrary finite index type N'.A1 (of cardinality card(N.A1) + 1), arbitrary state types N'.A3 n (not required to be finite or related to N.A3), and arbitrary initial state, update rule, and output map.
- In the dependency condition (1), the witness global states σ and σ' range over all functions (j : N'.A1) → N'.A3 j, not only global states reachable from the initial state N'.a4.
- Because (1) uses transitive closure (Relation.TransGen), at least one step is required even from an index to itself; also, Nonempty N'.A1 is stated explicitly in (1) even though it is already implied by (2).

divergences.description: Unconstrained per-unit state spaces and the '+1 unit' count: in S1, each unit's state type A3 n is an arbitrary Type (not required to be finite, and N' is not required to preserve N's per-unit state types). Thus N'.d13 = N.d13 + 1 bounds only the cardinality of the unit index set A1, while allowing N' to enlarge or replace unit state spaces arbitrarily (for example, packing auxiliary feedback channels into existing units or arbitrary state into the added unit).

Exact meaning of D11 relative to 'every unit lies on feedback loops with every unit': causal edges (D7/D8) are witnessed by arbitrary global states σ, σ' (including states unreachable from the initial state a4) and need not affect the output a6; moreover, strong connectivity with nonempty paths (∀ m n, Relation.TransGen N'.D8 m n) ensures that every pair of units lies on a closed directed walk (and every unit on a nonempty cycle, or self-loop if N has 0 units), not necessarily that every pair lies on a single simple cycle without repeated units.

Slight nuance in the characterization of the passages: while Appendix A (P-D57) starts from a feedforward network implementing a single-input map x → F(x) and P2's vice-versa half starts from a feedforward system, P-D53 states P2 informally for 'a given input-output function' without explicitly mentioning a time limit, and P-D52b remarks informally that Appendix A shows how to implement 'any function' (even though Appendix A itself starts from a feedforward network).

judgement.summary: The Lean TARGET accurately matches the author's description in quantifier structure, hypotheses, unit-count equality, strong-connectivity condition, and unbounded finite-history equivalence, and the description fairly reports what the cited passages claim and omit. Only minor caveats apply regarding S1's unconstrained per-unit state types, the exact graph-theoretic and interventional definition of D11, and minor nuances in the informal wording of P2 and P-D52b.
